basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Erat autem uterque nudus. Adam scilicet et uxor ejus, et non erubescebant. « Et merito,'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Erat autem uterque nudus. Adam scilicet et uxor ejus, et non erubescebant. « Et merito, quid enim puderet quando nullam legem senserant in membris suis repugnantem legi mentis suae? quae illos poena peccati post perpetrationem praevaricationis secuta est, usurpante inobedientia prohibitum, et justitia puniente commissum: quod antequam fieret, nudi erant, ut dictum est, et non confundebantur. Nullus erat motus in corpore, cui verecundia deberetur; nihil putabant velandum, quia nihil senserant refrenandum. »
